_doc: Work notes on the site, newest first by date. Each: date, title, slug, summary, grade (measured, derived, borrowed or hypothetical, and where); the body is site/notes/<slug>.html.

notes.title: In closed loop no adapter variant separates from the shipped adapter, and stock is 4 points behind it
notes.summary: Closed loop in the simulator on one truck and one driver: five arms (the shipped rig adapter, two lane-paint-plus-teacher variants without driver labels, an all-terms 2-minute variant, and stock with no adapter) on 30 held-out windows from 6 sessions, each run unpushed and pushed 1.0 and 1.5 m (120 pushed episodes per arm). Pushed recovery is 0.492 for shipped and 0.475 to 0.483 for the variants, with intervals about 6 points wide, so no variant separates from shipped and a loss of up to about 7 points is not excluded. Stock recovers 0.450, 4 points behind. Relative recovery is identical across arms on shared episodes, so these windows cannot separate models this close, and the recipe differences are not read as effects. One seed per arm; the adapter line is closed for the general goal.
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on recorded G55 drives: 30 held-out windows from 6 sessions, one training seed per arm, no per-episode rows saved, session intervals use 6 clusters. Two outside-model reviews; nothing deployed to the truck.
notes.result: no variant separates from shipped (recovered 0.475 to 0.483 against 0.492); stock 0.450

notes.title: Remembering a road helps planned speed, but it is route memory
notes.summary: Open loop on one truck and one driver. The rig adapter's gain is not memory of its training roads: adapted minus stock lateral plan error at 4 s is -0.017 m on roads over 200 m from the training drives, and the time-zero speed-scale gain holds on 17 of 17 drives there. Training 16 epochs instead of 4 did not improve the plan on trained roads. Plan error repeats weakly by place (correlation 0.29 against 0.06 for a shifted control). Blending the speed the driver held at the same place on earlier drives into stock's planned speed lowers 8 s speed error from 1.83 to 1.52 m/s on 11 of 13 drives. This is route memory: it helps only on road already driven, and it is not an improvement to the driving model. Two outside model reviews agreed. No model was trained on it and the branch is parked.
notes.grade: Measured open loop on recorded drives of one truck and one driver (17 drives for the adapter split, 13 for the speed blend), no closed-loop run; the wrong-place control is weak because it changes road type. Two outside-model reviews; nothing trained or deployed.
notes.result: remembered speed lowers 8 s planned speed error 1.83 to 1.52 m/s; route memory, not a model improvement

notes.title: The rig adapter's lane fix is mostly geometry; its plan and speed gains need the driver's labels, and two minutes of data over-trains
notes.summary: A measured account of the adapter recipe: 27 training runs and 3 stock scorings, open loop on 17 validation drives, mostly one seed. Stock fed the teacher's warp and shifted by the 0.239 m camera offset reaches right lane 0.042 m and left 0.086 m from paint (shipped adapter 0.034 m, 0.039 m), but its 4 s plan error is 0.420 m. Lane paint plus teacher with no driver labels matches the shipped lane result (0.034 m, 0.040 m). The shipped plan (0.352 m against stock 0.376 m) and speed (2.1% against 3.6%) gains need the path and speed labels, which also lower turn gain (0.829 against 0.853). Two minutes of one stretch over-trained at 63 epochs (plan 0.468 m, speed 8.1%) and did not at 6 epochs (0.378 m, 2.9%). No variant beats the shipped adapter except on turn gain. The lane truth is the same paint detector that made the training labels.
notes.grade: Measured open loop on 17 validation drives of recorded G55 drives, mostly one seed, no closed-loop run; lane truth is the same classical paint detector that made the training labels, scored on straight, clearly painted frames at 8 to 12 m. Two outside-model reviews; nothing deployed to the truck.
notes.result: no variant beats the shipped adapter; lane 0.034 / 0.039 m, plan 0.352 m, speed 2.1%

notes.title: Removing CPU warps, cold graph loads and single-GPU limits speeds training and simulation 2.6x to 107x
notes.summary: Measured before and after on two 230 W 24 GB GPUs with NVLink and 64 CPU cores: memory-mapped graph caching cut model load from 21.22 s to 1.24 s in FP32 (17.1x, 0.0 diff) and 19.12 s to 1.15 s in BF16 (16.7x); batched vmap in bfloat16 with float32 adapter weights cut a 4-epoch full-corpus adapter run from 3.41 h to 1.26 h (2.7x) within 1.6 mm on all 4,552 validation paint frames, and scaled to 200.3 samples/s across 2 GPUs with NVLink DDP (1.98x vs 1-GPU B=64 accumulation, 0.0 step-1 gradient diff); CUDA splatting, pull-push hole fill and grid_sample warps (cuda_fast) cut render time from 172.2 ms to 5.64 ms/view (30.6x) and 60-episode rollouts to 29.9 s across 2 GPUs (5.9x, matching aggregate recovery while diverging earlier than the CPU reference at trajectory level, onset p = 0.00098); and memory-mapped 5 Hz drive packs cut random-access ORT jump-ins from 1,385 ms to 13.0 ms (106.6x, 0.0 diff after a 149.2 s one-time pack build).
notes.grade: Measured on recorded G55 drives and dense closed-loop simulation windows with NVML hardware counters, gradient parity checks and trajectory-equivalence checks (cuda_fast fails step-by-step onset, p = 0.00098); CPU reference simulator unchanged.
notes.n: 31,555 refresh frames, 10 val drives, 60 sim episodes

notes.title: A rank-8 vision adapter puts lane lines within 3 to 5 cm of road paint and keeps push recovery when drives are balanced
notes.summary: Trained on 4 dual-camera visor-mount drives with comma's policy frozen and merged back into an ordinary ONNX file, a rank-8 low-rank adapter on N16's vision weights moved full-sequence validation lane-line error across all 10 unseen drives (60,787 steps, 4,552 paint frames) from 0.196 / 0.254 m (1.45 m warp) and 0.488 / 0.505 m (exact geometry) to 0.032 / 0.032 m (0.023 / 0.026 m on 2 locked hold-out drives, and 0.057 / 0.040 m unchanged on f22e06e5_56320). On the same 87 dense closed-loop windows (435 episodes per policy), the balanced 1.45 m adapter reached 71.6 to 72.4 % relative push recovery (+2.3 to +3.2 points over the 1.45 m baseline by window, 10-drive CIs touching or straddling zero; +4.6 to +5.5 points over a -0.239 m camera warp while holding within 0.005 to 0.021 m of centre); a 3-arm single-seed ablation showed uncapping an 88-minute highway drive (84.5 % of trainable steps and 3.7x total updates) cost 7.5 points of push recovery and adding open-loop turn supervision on the uncapped corpus cost a further 2.0 points.
notes.grade: Measured offline across all 60,787 5 Hz steps of 10 validation drives, 2 locked hold-out drives, the untouched 2026-11-10 road-paint script (1,384 to 1,529 frames per model), and 87 paired closed-loop windows; nothing deployed to the truck.
notes.result: lane error 0.032 / 0.032 m; 71.6 to 72.4 % rel. recovery

notes.title: N16 puts each lane line about 0.23 m too close to the camera on the truck
notes.summary: Against paint measured in the camera's own frames on the road plane, each of N16's inner lane lines is 0.21 m (highway, 34 and 42 frames) to 0.26 m (town, 102 frames) farther out than N16 puts it, the same at every distance from the camera from 0.55 to 2.15 m. A fixed outward move fitted on one road type leaves 0.03 to 0.06 m on the other; one scale leaves up to 0.18 m. The tablet's 3D scene now moves the lines out by 0.23 m and onto the truck's centreline; on 9 of 10 checked moments it draws them within 0.10 m of the paint, where before the right line was 0.41 to 0.51 m too close.
notes.grade: Measured on recorded G55 drives from the current camera mount: 178 straight-road frames from four drives, highway and town, by day. Inner lane lines only; road edges, curves and night not measured.
notes.result: each lane line 0.21 to 0.26 m outward of N16's

notes.title: The simulator could not draw highway views: one source frame every 0.2 s was too few
notes.summary: In the closed-loop simulator, 35 of 95 windows at 30 to 33 m/s and 18 of 24 at 33 to 36 m/s ended the unpushed episode in a view it could not draw, and none between 12 and 24 m/s. The view is warped from a recorded frame kept every 0.2 s, up to 6.6 m behind the truck at 33 m/s; warped past about 6 m the near road is left empty. Drawing from every recorded frame cut such endings from 61 of 160 unpushed episodes to 1 on the same 80 windows. They had been scored as the model failing to recover.
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on recorded G55 drives from after the camera re-aim: 320 windows for the speed table, 2,880 warps of real frames on 80 windows for coverage, 80 windows for the before and after. A correction to the method; the model comparison it interrupted is not finished.
notes.result: undrawn unpushed episodes 61 of 160, then 1 of 160

notes.title: comma's 2026-11-05 model recovers more pushes than N16 in the simulator
notes.summary: Untrained, comma's f22e06e5_56320 recovered 49.3 to 69.5 % of pushed episodes on 73 validation windows from 9 drives, against 40.8 to 58.6 % for N16 (+7.2 to +11.0 points; the doublet interval includes zero). At three times the residual scale its gain over N16 at 3x was +4.8 to +8.2 points, every validation interval including zero. Unpushed, it ends 0.07 to 0.16 m right of the driver's path.
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on recorded G55 drives, 9 validation and 2 hold-out drives, all from before the camera re-aim; untrained, no bar set in advance, nothing deployed.
notes.result: +7.2 to +11.0 points over N16 as shipped

notes.title: Imitation training of N16's residual head did not beat its untrained start
notes.summary: Trained in the simulator to copy an oracle's steering on the states it visits (DAgger), N16's residual head recovered more pushes on its two training drives but did not beat the untrained 3x start on 9 validation and 2 hold-out drives. There its unpushed line sat 0.14 to 0.37 m left of the driver's path; a follow-up check ties that shift to the camera being re-aimed between the training and the evaluation drives.
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on recorded G55 drives: 2 training, 9 validation and 2 hold-out drives, and a check on 3 locked-test drives with nothing claimed; a negative result, nothing deployed.

notes.title: N16's residual head at two to four times its scale recovers more pushes
notes.summary: Untrained, N16 with comma's residual steering head at three times its shipped scale recovered 52.7 to 68.5 % of pushed episodes on 73 validation windows from 9 drives, against 40.8 to 58.6 % as shipped (+7.9 to +27.7 points, every 95 % interval over drives above zero). Most of the gain is fewer episodes leaving the area the simulator can draw. Corrected 2026-11-09: the first slow-drift run pushed 1.6 times the stated distance; its figures here are from a rerun.
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on recorded G55 drives, 9 validation and 2 hold-out drives; untrained, locked test not run, nothing deployed (the truck runs scale 1).

notes.title: A trained steering correction on N16 recovers more often in simulation
notes.summary: On 44 held-out simulator windows, a TD3-trained correction on N16 recovered from 1.5 m pushes 0.76 of the time against 0.58 for its untrained starting point (+0.18 [+0.13, +0.33]). Against the driver's recorded line the gain was +0.07 at 1.5 m and +0.01 at 1.0 m.
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on recorded G55 drives, 3 held-out drives; exploratory, locked test not run, nothing deployed.

notes.title: Camera position moves where N16 holds the truck in its lane
notes.summary: In simulation, moving N16's virtual camera sideways moves its held lane position by -0.97 m per metre of shift. A road-plane warp for a lens 0.239 m right of centre took back about half of the +0.191 m median shift in the hold and restored 0.394 of 1.0 m pushes against 0.197 uncorrected (base 0.509).
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on recorded G55 drives (135 dev day windows, mirror-mount windows emulating the visor mount); not tested on a real drive.
notes.result: -0.97 m per m of camera shift

notes.title: N16's frozen vision tokens do not replace a box detector
notes.summary: A head on N16's frozen vision tokens found 2.7 % of vehicles at IoU 0.5, against 55.5 % for YOLO26s on the same frames. Added to the box, the tokens gave a speed error of 3.88 to 4.44 m/s against 2.31 m/s for the analytical tracker.
notes.grade: Measured offline on recorded G55 drives with hand-checked and hindsight truth; exploratory, one head configuration, nothing deployed.

notes.title: The camera loop ran below 20 Hz because OpenBLAS threads spun
notes.summary: On N16 drives the camera loop ran 17.7 to 18.8 Hz: a serial decoder skipped ticks while OpenBLAS worker threads used 1.75 cores. With one OpenBLAS thread per service, three drives held 19.91 to 19.92 Hz.
notes.grade: Measured on recorded drives, in replay on the truck's Jetson board, and on three drives after the fix was installed.

notes.title: comma's models turn the wrong way first because of the base policy
notes.summary: In 258 of 258 pushes where a full comma model first steered with the push, its residual-off copy did too. The residual removes 61-88% of these turns but sits at its 1.0 m/s² bound on the rest.
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on recorded G55 drives with comma's own residual-off files; exploratory, one seed, daytime reprojection only, not a deployed change.

notes.title: After a push, N16 still encodes the truck's offset and heading
notes.summary: A linear probe reads the truck's lateral offset from N16's vision tokens at R² 0.84-0.93 and from its base summary at 0.87-0.98 on held-out sessions. The wrong-way first turn comes from the base's readout of yaw rate, not from missing information.
notes.grade: Measured in open-loop simulation on recorded G55 drives; exploratory, daytime stock-lens windows and N16 only, not a deployed change.

notes.title: Teaching comma's world model to keep a sideways offset
notes.summary: By day comma's world model as shipped already puts the road at a commanded offset (road gain 1.05 at 3 s). Fine-tuning made it overshoot (1.24), reward training did not pass its gate, and no version holds the road at night.
notes.grade: Measured in simulation on recorded G55 drives; exploratory, small test sets, not a deployed change.

notes.title: A truck model learned from the G55's CAN predicts motion better
notes.summary: On 12 held-out drives a recurrent network learned from the truck's CAN data has a sideways error of 0.29 m after 4 s of free running, against 7.34 m for the hand-built model and 0.66 m for the same equations refit. It fails a stopping check, so the simulator's default stays hand-built.
notes.grade: Measured on recorded G55 drives, with the test set scored once per candidate; exploratory, one truck configuration, no steering actuator.
